gap: No result ChatGPT got prices any of the models it compares, and none says that Sabrent's own US store lists the $299.99 SB-TB4K Thunderbolt 4 KVM, which ChatGPT carded as 'Best Thunderbolt 4', as unavailable today (2026-11-10). On maker stores today the field runs from $169.99 (AV Access KD-E10) to $699.00 (TESmart HDC202-X24).
standout_why: I read three pages in full: the two Dock Gear HQ pages ChatGPT cited (best-docking-stations-with-built-in-kvm-switch-2026 and best-kvm-switches-for-dual-monitor-setups-2026) and the cited ThunderboltLaptop best-dual-monitor-kvm-switches page. None of the three gives a single dollar figure; each says only 'Check price on Amazon'. ThunderboltLaptop calls the StarTech 'the most expensive' without a number. None of them flags the Sabrent stock status. Their spec and weakness points (Mac mirroring with MST, DisplayLink drivers, 60W to the active host only) already appear in these cited pages, so those points alone would score 0–1. What is new is the full set of prices from today and the Sabrent availability.
decides: Prices from today change the shortlist for some setups. For a Mac plus a second laptop that needs two extended screens, the IOGEAR Dock Pro Duo is $299.95 at IOGEAR's store against ChatGPT's $326.59 StarTech 129N. Dock Gear HQ says the IOGEAR charges both hosts at 100W, while the StarTech gives 90W to the active host and 45W to the other. Both need DisplayLink. A Mac user who wants native video (no DisplayLink) can buy the AV Access iDock M10 for $289.99, but only on an M3 with the lid closed, a Pro/Max chip, or an M4. AV Access says M1/M2 support only one external display. The Sabrent pick should be dropped or flagged because its maker store lists it as unavailable. The $259.99 AV Access iDock C20 stays the two-Windows-laptop pick, and the $169.99 KD-E10 stays the laptop-plus-desktop value pick.
